content.thinking: This looks like a clear upstream dependency failure - api.io-pay.example is returning 503 errors.

hypotheses.subject: api.io-pay.example
hypotheses.summary: At 09:15 the payment provider api.io-pay.example began returning HTTP 503 for /v1/shoppers/{id}/card, and io-shop's account page path propagated those failures: error rate jumped from ~1% to 64.5% then 100%, with latency rising from ~45ms p50 to ~2045ms (timeout/retry against the failing upstream). No deploys or config changes to io-shop in the preceding week, and traffic and memory were flat, so the failure arrived through the dependency.

hypotheses.subject: api.io-pay.example
hypotheses.summary: Alternative reading: the 503s could come from an io-shop-side misconfiguration of the payment provider endpoint/credential (wrong host, path or key) rather than the provider itself being down. Nothing in the change log supports this — no deploy or config revision is recorded in the week before onset — so it is only a fallback if the provider proves healthy.
